outputs.explanation: Scatter plot in which each of the n=141 samples is shown as its own marker (shape/color coded by cell line/subtype); the marginal histograms summarize the distribution of these same individual points. Individual data underlying the plot are directly visible.

Each point plotted is a per-cell-line mean (mean ± s.d. of 6 samples per reporter, per the caption) rather than an individual replicate measurement, and no overlay of the individual replicate values is shown alongside the averaged points/error bars.
These are fitted density (line) curves showing distributions of period/amplitude values; line/density plots are exempt from requiring an overlay of individual data points.
Box plots of CWT ridge lengths, and individual reporter data points (Per2-Luc and Bmal1-Luc, colored dots) are overlaid on each box, in addition to being an inherently exempt plot type.

Polar histograms display the distribution of phase-difference values (binned frequency/probability representation), a distribution-type plot analogous to a histogram, which does not require an additional overlay of individual points.
Polar histogram summarizing subtype-averaged phase differences; as a histogram/distribution-style plot it falls into the exempt category not requiring individual point overlays.
This panel shows a single illustrative example trace and fitted model (a schematic/example plot), not an averaged summary statistic across samples, so individual data point overlay is not applicable.

Scatter plot where each of the n=117 samples is shown as an individual marker (error bars reflect fitting uncertainty for that sample, not variability across replicates), so individual data points are already directly displayed.
